holidays.name: International Lefthanders Day
holidays.description: A day for the roughly 10% of people who do everything a little backwards. Lefties are invited to celebrate their dominant hand. Righties get a chance to think about a world full of right-handed scissors, spiral notebooks and can openers.
holidays.origin: Lefthanders International founded the observance in 1976. It was meant to raise awareness of the everyday struggles and unique traits of left-handed people. It is now celebrated around the world.
holidays.funFact: The word 'sinister' comes from the Latin word for 'left'. For centuries, left-handedness was wrongly linked with bad luck and suspicion.

holidays.name: National Filet Mignon Day
holidays.description: A day to treat yourself to one of the most tender cuts of beef. Steakhouses and home grillers mark it with a thick, buttery, fork-tender steak, ideally with a little bacon wrapped around it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a yearly excuse for steak lovers to indulge.
holidays.funFact: 'Filet mignon' is French for 'dainty fillet'. The cut comes from the tenderloin, a muscle that does very little work, which is why it is so tender.
